programme: No recognisable module spans the twelve factors. They fall into at least five unrelated functional classes: a nuclear-receptor steroidogenesis regulator (SF1, targets CYP11A1/HSD3B2/STAR/MC2R/SULT2A1 — the classic adrenal/gonadal steroidogenic programme); a Th2/epithelial-differentiation TF (GATA3, targets IL4/IL5/IL13/IL7R/RAG1); a PRC2 Polycomb component (JARID2, targets CCND1/RB1/CDK4/NOTCH1/SETDB1/EHMT2); a NuRD chromatin-remodelling factor (MTA1, targets MMP9/TP53/TNF/IL1B/CDKN1A); two RAS-MAPK/ETS effectors (CIC and ELK3, targets ETV5/RASA1/JUN/EGR1/FOS/VEGFA); a general-transcription-initiation factor normally restricted to spermatogenesis (TBPL1, targets GTF2B/GTF2A1); senescence/apoptosis chromatin factors (HMGB2, BCLAF1, targets BAX/TP73/MDM2/TP53/SIRT1); and homeodomain/zinc-finger developmental regulators (HOXA5, ZNF219, SP2). None of these share a named complex, and their target lists barely overlap (TP53 and CDKN1A recur across several, but as generic stress/cell-cycle nodes, not a specific programme).
role_in_a: not applicable — no single programme is carried by enough of these factors to assign it a role in Alzheimer's disease
role_in_b: not applicable — no single programme is carried by enough of these factors to assign it a role in psoriasis
shared_axis: None identified. The factors do not converge on one pathway, so no mechanistic axis can be proposed that would explain why brain and skin tissue would share this specific set.
reasoning: Twelve factors spanning steroidogenesis, Th2/epidermal differentiation, Polycomb repression, NuRD remodelling, RAS-MAPK signalling, core transcription initiation, and senescence/apoptosis do not constitute a mechanism — they are a list, not a module. The one factor with genuine literature placement in both tissues, GATA3, is documented in psoriasis for epidermal keratinocyte differentiation and in immunity for Th2 polarization, neither of which connects to the chromatin/steroidogenic/MAPK factors also on the list. Forcing a story here would be the over-generous reading the task warns against; the honest read is that this pair's target-set concordance is not explained by a shared regulatory programme.
support: none found — no retrieved paper connects any of these factors to both Alzheimer's disease and psoriasis, and none support a shared mechanism across the set
how_to_falsify: Test whether the closest candidate sub-pair, CIC and ELK3 (both RAS-MAPK/ETS-pathway effectors), show correlated target-gene activity changes in matched Alzheimer's brain and psoriatic skin samples; if their bound/regulated target sets significantly co-vary across the two tissues beyond what is expected from generic MAPK activity, that would argue for a real shared module and against 'incoherent'.
caveats: Brain–skin pairing, 64 patient-group comparisons over 6 independent cohort pairs. GATA3 is the only factor with Open Targets association recorded in both diseases (AD percentile 0.81, psoriasis percentile 0.74) and with disease-specific literature on both sides, but its psoriasis role (keratinocyte differentiation) and typical immune role (Th2) do not obviously connect to Alzheimer's. Most other factors have Open Targets association or literature support in Alzheimer's disease only, with nothing recorded for psoriasis. NR3C1, an obvious candidate for a shared steroid/immune axis, was excluded on two independent grounds (single-view recurrence 0.28, and tissue-generic percentile 0.909) — its absence is the reason no such axis appears here, not an oversight.
